title: Zayin Hebrew Letter (ז): Sound & Words
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Zayin (ז): its [z] sound, with example words like זְבוּב (fly) and זֶה (this), plus interactive practice.

editorialIssues.detail: One letter-recognition distractor set uses letters (Resh, Nun) not introduced in this lesson. Beginner scaffolding can be improved separately from the approved source synchronization.

blocks.text: Zayin Hebrew Letter (ז): Sound, Words & Practice
Zayin (ז) is the seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Its name is pronounced 'zayin.' In modern Hebrew, the letter represents [z], like the 'z' in the English word 'zoo.'

The Hebrew word זְבוּב [zvuv] means 'fly' (the insect) and has one syllable. It has four letters: Zayin (ז), Bet (ב), Vav (ו), and Bet (ב) again. In modern Hebrew, the initial Sheva is not pronounced as a separate vowel here, so the word begins [zv]. Both Bet letters have no Dagesh and represent [v]. Vav with Shuruk (וּ) supplies the vowel [u].

The Hebrew word (זֶה) [ze], which translates to 'this' or 'this is' in English, consists of only two distinct letters: Zayin (ז) and Hey (ה). A Segol beneath the Zayin produces the [e] sound. The letter Hey has no vowel and, in this case, is silent at the end of the word.
The Hebrew phrase זֶה אַבָּא [ze a-ba] consists of two familiar words: זֶה ('this') and אַבָּא ('dad' or 'father'). Together, they mean 'This is Dad.'
You've learned the seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet, Zayin. We've learned two new words and a phrase that use Zayin. Now, let's practice to really remember it.

exercises.prompt: Find the letter 'Zayin' among the given Hebrew letters.
exercises.explanation: The Hebrew letter Zayin (ז) is the seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet. It represents the [z] sound, like in the English word 'zebra.'

exercises.prompt: Does the letter Zayin (זֶ) marked with Segol produce the [ze] sound?
exercises.explanation: Segol represents the [e] sound, and when combined with Zayin (זֶ), it produces [ze].

exercises.prompt: How do you pronounce the Hebrew word for 'this' (זֶה)?
exercises.explanation: The Hebrew word 'זֶה' consists of Zayin (ז) with Segol, producing [ze], and Hey (ה), which is silent in this case. Together, they form [ze].

exercises.prompt: How do you pronounce the letter Hey (הָ) when marked with Kamatz Gadol?
exercises.explanation: Kamatz Gadol represents [a] in modern Hebrew. When combined with Hey (הָ), it produces [ha].

exercises.prompt: Does the letter Zayin (זָ) marked with Kamatz Gadol produce the [za] sound?
exercises.explanation: Kamatz Gadol represents the [a] sound. When combined with Zayin (זָ), it produces [za].

exercises.prompt: How is Bet (ב) without Dagesh pronounced, as at the end of זְבוּב?
exercises.explanation: Bet without Dagesh represents [v], like the final sound in 'love.' Bet with Dagesh (בּ) represents [b].

The word זָהָב means 'gold' and has two syllables: [za-hav]. Zayin with Kamatz Gadol (זָ) produces [za], Hey with Kamatz Gadol (הָ) produces [ha], and the final Bet without Dagesh represents [v]. The final [v] closes the second syllable.

exercises.prompt: How is the letter Bet (בַ) without Dagesh and marked with Patah pronounced?
exercises.explanation: Patah represents [a] in modern Hebrew. When combined with Bet (בַ) without Dagesh, it produces [va].

exercises.prompt: Does Vav (וֹ) with Holam Male produce the [vi] sound?
exercises.explanation: Holam Male (וֹ) represents [o]. Keep the vowel steady; the English vowel in 'goat' is only an approximation. This form does not produce [vi].

exercises.prompt: How is the letter Gimel (גָ) pronounced when marked with Kamatz Gadol?
exercises.explanation: Kamatz Gadol represents the [a] sound. When combined with Gimel (גָ), it produces [ga].

exercises.prompt: In modern Hebrew, does Zayin (ז) represent the [ts] sound?
exercises.explanation: In modern Hebrew, Zayin (ז) represents [z], like the 'z' in 'zoo.' It does not represent [ts].
The Hebrew word for 'fly' (the insect) is זְבוּב [zvuv]. It has one syllable.

exercises.prompt: What is the correct transliteration of the Hebrew word זֶה?
exercises.explanation: The word זֶה is transliterated as 'ze,' meaning 'this' or 'this is.'

exercises.prompt: Which Hebrew phrase means 'This is Dad'?
exercises.explanation: The Hebrew phrase זֶה אַבָּא [ze a-ba] means 'This is Dad.'
